**Voica v0.6.3 — an installer, and reasoning models no longer talk over your dictation.**

### New: an installer

The release page has had two executables and no way for you to know which one you needed — the
answer depended on whether the .NET 8 Desktop Runtime was installed. **`Voica-Setup-0.6.3.exe`**
removes the question: it carries the self-contained build, installs for your user only (so **no UAC
prompt**), adds a Start-menu entry and a normal uninstall record, and offers to close a running copy
when you install over it. Uninstalling removes the program and **keeps your data** — history,
settings and the API key stay in `%APPDATA%\Voica`.

The two bare executables stay for anyone who prefers a single file with no installation.

### Fixed

- **Reasoning leaked into your text.** Some chat models put their thinking into the answer, wrapped
  in `<think>…</think>`. All of it was being delivered instead of your dictation. This was not
  exotic: `qwen/qwen3.6-27b` is the second choice for AI term correction, so anyone whose
  `openai/gpt-oss-120b` is blocked for their Groq organization hit it every time. Measured against
  the live model: 3800–11500 characters of reasoning per answer, now stripped.
- **A rambling answer can no longer replace your text** — correction swaps words, so anything empty
  or more than twice as long is discarded and the original is delivered.
- **`allam-2-7b`** (an Arabic model that happened to sort first alphabetically) is no longer picked
  as the fallback for correcting Russian terms.
- **`--test-all` no longer resets your settings** — it used to switch AI term correction off.

### Install

Windows 10 1809+ / x64:

| File | Size | Needs |
|---|---|---|
| **`Voica-Setup-0.6.3.exe`** | ~75 MB | nothing — recommended |
| `Voica.exe` | ~80 MB | nothing — single file, no installation |
| `Voica-fx.exe` | ~37 MB | [.NET 8 Desktop Runtime](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet/8.0) installed once |

Not code-signed yet, so SmartScreen may warn → **More info → Run anyway**
([why, and how to verify](https://github.com/Inhum/voica-win#why-does-windows-warn-about-this-app)).

Full changelog: https://github.com/Inhum/voica-win/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md
